name: IL-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: 6-point Democratic district lean plus favorable national environment
Incumbent Bill Foster with $2.5M cash on hand vs. challenger's $23K
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
No independent polling of the race
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Foster: a D+6 district, incumbency, a large financial advantage, and markets pricing a Democratic win near certain. With no contrary polling or ratings, the baseline margin of about 19 points stands.
model.watch: A late surge in Republican outside spending or unexpectedly strong national headwinds for Democrats could tighten the race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bill Foster, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a suburban Chicago district that leans Democratic by about six points. He enters the general election with roughly $2.5 million on hand after raising over $2.1 million, while Republican Jeff Walter has raised about $311,000 and holds only about $23,000 in cash. No outside groups are opposing Foster, and no independent polls of the race are available.

Prediction markets give Foster roughly a 96 percent chance of winning, and the fundamentals point the same way: the district lean, incumbency, and the money gap all favor the Democrat. With no expert raters flagging the race and no contrary polling, this sits firmly in Safe D territory, though the absence of direct polling leaves some room for uncertainty about the exact margin.
